threads.body: [General] This restores only the OpenTelemetry element found in the delegate's `CoroutineContext`, which is not necessarily the effective parent context. For example, this module's `TestContextElement` intentionally runs after the automatic OpenTelemetry element and can make a different context current; after this wrapper completes, the delegate will instead resume under the stale automatic context, so subsequent spans get the wrong parent. Capture `Context.current()` before starting/opening the `WithSpan` span and pass that exact parent context to the wrapper (or otherwise update the full delegate thread context), and cover this combination with a regression test.

[Testing] The new continuation path explicitly decodes a failed Kotlin `Result` and ends the span with that error, but the added regression test covers only successful completion. Add a tail-delegated `@WithSpan` method whose callee suspends and then throws, and assert that the span completes with error status and the exception event; this also validates the Kotlin `Result` bridge across supported versions.

`BaseContinuationImpl.getCallerFrame()` returns null when the completion is not a `CoroutineStackFrame`, so this wrapper truncates coroutine stack-trace recovery and `DebugProbes` dumps at every tail-delegated `@WithSpan` call. kotlinx-coroutines solves this in its own equivalent wrapper `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.internal.StackFrameContinuation`: also implement `CoroutineStackFrame`, return `delegate` from `getCallerFrame()` when it is one, and null from `getStackTraceElement()`.

[Testing] `Nothing` here makes the compiler emit a `KotlinNothingValueException` guard after the suspend call, so `annotatedFailure` gets a state machine and the instrumentation takes the pre-existing `exitCoroutine` path. `ContextContinuation.resumeWith` and the `KotlinResultUtilKt.exceptionOrNull` bridge stay uncovered, and the test passes either way. Dropping the return type makes `annotatedFailure` a tail call.


[General] `intercepted()` only unwraps a `ContinuationImpl`, so it returns this wrapper unchanged. When a tail-optimized `@WithSpan` method suspends through `suspendCancellableCoroutine` or `suspendCoroutine`, the resulting `CancellableContinuationImpl` holds this wrapper instead of a `DispatchedContinuation`, and `DispatchedTask.dispatch` then falls back to resuming the caller directly on the completing thread rather than dispatching it back to its own dispatcher. `ScopeCoroutine.afterCompletion` depends on the same interception. Please keep the continuation interceptable and cover it with a cross-thread dispatcher test.

replies.body:
While this is a valid issue, I don't think it can be easily solved with this (limited) approach. Expanding to cover that issue (without breaking existing regression tests) would require even deeper integration with Kotlin's coroutine resumption mechanism.

Since this issue is kinda niche, I'm leaning towards keeping this PR as-is to fix the previous issue and tackle this with a redesign later.
